title: Correctness of the De Morgan gadget
statement: Fix natural numbers $n$ and $K$. For every gate $g$ and finite list $G$ of gates, assume that each argument of the $i$th gate of $G$ is less than $n+i$, and each argument of $g$ is less than $n+|G|$. Assume also that if $g$ is a NOT gate then it has exactly one argument, and that the number of arguments of $g$ is at most $K$. The De Morgan construction applied to $g$ after $G$ produces a gate list extending $G$ and an output vertex whose index is less than $n$ plus the length of the resulting list. The resulting list is acyclic, and on every Boolean input the output vertex has the value of $g$ evaluated on the values obtained by running $G$ on that input. The resulting list has length at most $|G|+|g	ext{'s argument list}|+2$, the output depth is at most three plus the maximum depth of the vertices read by $g$ (taking this maximum to be zero when there are no arguments), and every added gate is well formed, is not an OR gate, and has at most $\max(1,K)$ arguments.
